subject: Post-call: EdgeFin performance / SLO qualification & benchmark methodology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@edgefin.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: EdgeFin performance / SLO qualification & benchmark methodology

Thanks again for the time today, Alex — really helpful call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a reproducible benchmark run that validates your latency and throughput targets.

Recap (per our call)
- Primary goal: ensure the model+serving configuration meets your latency SLOs at 95th and 99th percentiles for single-turn generation (50–150 tokens). Target: p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 400ms.
- Throughput / concurrency: baseline traffic is ~120 qps sustained during peak; peak bursts up to 600 qps for ~5–10 minute windows.
- Streaming: partial token streaming for interactive UI is required; client expects first-token latency <80ms for cached prompts.
- Quality constraints: output quality must be consistent with your in-house eval set; we’ll preserve same prompts/eval harness.

Proposed next steps
1) Share a small sample prompt set and an anonymized evaluation harness (prompts + expected outputs). You mentioned you could send an export — thanks in advance.
2) We’ll run a controlled benchmark using Redwood’s bench-run harness (reproducible, deterministic seed, and configurable concurrency/sequence-length distributions). We’ll measure p50/p95/p99, tail jitter, throughput, and stream-first-token latency.
3) Schedule a 2-hour benchmark session where we run: baseline (no caching), with prefix/KV cache, batching at several sizes, and a streaming configuration.
4) Deliver a results report with reproducible config, raw logs, and suggested production config (batching, quantization, routing).

Attached: redwood-benchmark-template-v1.xlsx with measurement definitions and the JSON/CSV format we expect for prompts.

Questions for you
- Can you confirm the p95/p99 targets above?
- Can you provide a small (50–200) prompt sample and the evaluation harness export? Preferably as CSV/S3 link.
- Any restrictions on data going to hosted infrastructure (e.g., must run in your VPC)?

If you’re good with that, we can tentatively schedule the benchmark for next Wed/Thu (Aug 31 / Sep 1) in your timezone — we’ll need a 2-hour window and an optional extra hour for troubleshooting.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

--

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: EdgeFin performance / SLO qualification & benchmark methodology

Thanks for the prompt sample, Alex — that’s perfect to start. A few technical clarifications so the results are reproducible and comparable: please see inline.

Measurement definitions (we’ll use these exact definitions in our report)
- p50/p95/p99: measured on end-to-end server-side response completion time (server accept -> last byte of final token emitted). For streaming, we’ll also measure first-byte latency (server accept -> first token byte).
- Tail jitter: 95th->99th delta distribution over 1-minute windows.
- Throughput: measured as successful responses/sec at target latency thresholds; we’ll also record max sustainable QPS per configuration before >1% errors or p99 > your threshold.
- Reproducibility: bench-run will use deterministic RNG seed and record all run configurations in the artifacts. We’ll provide the exact invocation and Docker image sha.

Benchmark harness / artifacts we need from you
- Full eval harness export (CSV/JSON) or S3 link for the 1k prompt set and expected outputs.
- Expected sequence length distribution (if not in the CSV).
- If you have warm/cold cache expectations, indicate that — we’ll run both cold-start and warmed runs.

Redwood-side notes
- We’ll run bench-run v2 (attached benchmark-harness-instructions.md). It supports streaming measurements and concurrent connection emulation.
- For streaming-first-byte latency tests we recommend a client-side shim to avoid client rendering jitter; if you can share a small client harness that reproduces your UI pipeline we’ll include it.

Access & environment
- For the initial run we can use Redwood-hosted staging creds. If you prefer to keep artifacts in your S3, share a temp presigned URL.
- If we need to run inside your VPC, we’ll need a short checklist (network ACLs, IAM role) — happy to sync on that if it becomes necessary.

I’ll plan to prep a benchmark matrix covering: no-cache baseline, prefix cache enabled, batching at [8, 16, 32], and streaming with varying max in-flight tokens.

-Marissa / Rishi (cc Monica)

Rishi Malhotra
Technical Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

- Sequence-length distribution: attached in the S3 as metadata (avg 90 tokens, 10% at 250+ tokens).
- Warm vs cold: our production cluster benefits substantially from KV cache for frequently seen prompts; please run both cold (fresh instance) and warmed (preload cache with 100k recent prefixes).
- Streaming shim: our frontend team can provide a small Node.js client that reproduces the rendering pipeline — I’ll include that in the S3 export.

Schedule
- We’re available for the benchmark window next Wed (31 Aug) 0900–1200 PT or Thu (1 Sep) 1300–1600 PT. Please pick a 2-hour slot and we’ll arrange access.

Access & NDA
- NDA: I can get the formal one signed today if Redwood needs it before we hand over S3 access.
- For the initial run we’re OK with Redwood-hosted staging; if the results look promising we’ll discuss Dedicated/private deployment.

Attachments to come: presigned S3 link and a brief README (I’ll post to the thread).

—Alex
